source.name: Cato Brand Hub
source.note: Machine-readable summary for course runtime, linting and tests. The hub stays canonical; re-check it before major releases. PMS/CMYK values marked TBD on the hub are omitted.

rules: Core greens establish the foundation; secondary colors support emphasis and illustration and never compete with the greens.
Neutral greys create backgrounds, separation and readable hierarchy with sufficient contrast.
Gradients add depth and direct focus; they are not decoration.
Highlight Green belongs on dark surfaces or large display type; it fails contrast as small text on white.

color.use: Preferred mark on light, neutral backgrounds

white.use: On Cato Green, dark green, black and imagery

rules: Use only official artwork. Do not redraw, recolor, distort, rotate or separate the logo elements.
Give the mark clear space so it stays recognizable at every size.
Color or black mark on light surfaces; white mark on dark surfaces.

forms.solidDisc: Boldest expression; a clear focal point.
forms.openRing: Foundational form; connection, continuity and the unified platform.
forms.doubleRing: Inner ring is the customer's network; outer ring is the protection Cato provides.
forms.concentricRings: Movement, energy and scale; each ring reflects a core pillar.

rules: Flat 2D only. The dimensional 3D ring treatment is retired.
Most recognizable in Cato Green; use it as a focal point, frame or backdrop, with restraint.
The Ring may frame, crop or silhouette relevant imagery while its silhouette stays recognizable.
Outline icons are the primary treatment for diagrams, editorial content and product explanations.
Solid icons only to give one idea more weight; not a second default set.
Isometric illustration only for architecture and relationships, never as a substitute for simple icons.
Icons are conceptual; they are not product marks or evidence of a specific feature or commitment.

photography: Authentic, human, contemporary; avoid staged, generic or traditional stock compositions.
Create a clear focal point with selective focus and thoughtful composition.
Use perspective, scale and sightlines to express clarity.
Abstract movement imagery (connectivity, light, data) instead of familiar cyber clichés.

designPrinciples.name: Reveal what matters
designPrinciples.rule: Use hierarchy, contrast, layering and space to make the primary message immediately clear.

designPrinciples.name: Connect ideas
designPrinciples.rule: Show relationships through grouping, proximity, pathways and framing. Visuals add meaning, not decoration.

designPrinciples.name: Resolve with clarity
designPrinciples.rule: Use grids, alignment, containment and precision to guide toward a clear takeaway or action.

voice.summary: Clear, confident and human: clarity without simplification, intelligence without ego, confidence without alarm, authority without corporate stiffness.

principles.name: Clear, not complicated
principles.rule: Plain language, strong hierarchy and a clear point over showing how technical we can be.

principles.name: Calmly confident
principles.rule: No fear or drama. Focus on what people can understand, control and do next.

principles.name: Smart and decisive
principles.rule: Explain what it means and what to do next, with a clear point of view.

principles.name: Human and conversational
principles.rule: Write for people, not at them, in natural language.

standards.precedence: Cato conventions first; Chicago for style and usage; Merriam-Webster for spelling.

productNameNotes: The hub also lists bare 'Cato SASE' as incorrect where the platform is meant; use 'Cato SASE Platform'. The linter flags it for review rather than blocking, because 'Cato SASE' can appear legitimately inside longer phrases.
Validate current product and component names with Product Marketing before customer-facing or contractual use.
